case_title: PATTU RAJAN v. STATE OF TAMIL NADU
accused_occupation: Proprietor of a chain of hotels
confession: Confession of accused no.6 relied on
high_court_outcome: Modified conviction under s.304 Part-I to one under s.302
neutral_facts: The accused, who was the proprietor of a chain of hotels, abducted the victim and his wife, then later murdered the victim to marry the wife. The victim's wife provided detailed testimony about the accused's intentions and actions, including the abduction and subsequent murder. The accused were identified through circumstantial evidence, including the recovery of personal belongings and the identification of the victim's body. The accused were also linked through hotel records and the recovery of a wallet containing the victim's photograph. The prosecution's case was supported by the testimony of multiple witnesses, including the victim's wife and her mother, as well as the identification of the body through various methods, including superimposition tests. The accused were found to have taken the victim away in a car and murdered him, then disposed of the body in a forest area.
